title: How would you design a real-time chat / messaging system (e.g. WhatsApp/Slack): why persist the message to the DB BEFORE delivering it, WebSockets (full-duplex) vs long-polling for delivery, guaranteeing per-conversation message ordering, delivery vs read receipts, presence/typing indicators, offline users (queue + push notification), multi-device sync, and how do you scale stateful WebSocket servers (sticky sessions / a shared pub-sub like Redis so a message published on one server reaches a socket on another)?
shortTitle: How would you design a real-time chat / messaging system like WhatsApp or Slack
keyPoints: Persist first, deliver second: the database is the source of truth, and delivery is a projection of what is already stored.
WebSockets provide full-duplex persistent connections for instant bidirectional message delivery.
Per-conversation ordering uses a monotonic sequence number assigned at persist time, not global ordering.
Delivery and read are two distinct state transitions tracked per recipient per message.
Offline users receive a push notification; on reconnect the client replays from its last-seen sequence.
Scaling stateful WebSocket servers uses sticky sessions plus Redis pub-sub fan-out across servers.
Deduplicate with a client-generated message ID so retries never create duplicate messages.

s1_definition.oneliner: Persist first then deliver, use WebSockets for live full-duplex delivery with a Redis pub-sub fan-out across servers, order per conversation with a sequence number, and fall back to queue plus push for offline users.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Persist first** – Write the message to durable storage and assign its sequence before acknowledging the sender or delivering to anyone.
- **WebSockets** – A persistent full-duplex channel where server and client send frames any time without re-establishing.
- **Sequence number** – A monotonic counter per conversation assigns at persist time; clients render by sequence, not arrival time.
- **Receipts** – Delivery (reached device) and read (user opened) are separate states per recipient.
- **Offline** – Message already persisted; enqueue delivery + push notification; replay on reconnect.
- **Scaling** – Sticky sessions pin a user to a server; Redis pub-sub lets a message arriving on server B reach a socket on server A.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India's secure messaging, when Rajesh sends a message to his relationship manager Priya, the bank first writes it in the permanent ledger and only then says "sent". If Priya is online, a dedicated open phone line (WebSocket) delivers it instantly. If she is away, the message waits in her inbox and her phone buzzes. The bank stamps each message with a running number per conversation so they always appear in the right order.

sections.s6_takeaway:
A real-time chat system is built around one rule above all: persist the message to durable storage and assign its sequence before acknowledging the sender or delivering to anyone. At National Bank of India, a bug where messages were delivered before persisting caused Rajesh's messages to Priya to be lost on a crash. Persist-first fixed that permanently because the database is the source of truth and delivery is just a projection.

For live transport, Pankaj uses WebSockets for full-duplex instant delivery, with long-polling as a fallback. Ordering is guaranteed per conversation with a monotonic sequence number assigned at persist time, so even if the network reorders delivery, the display is always correct. Delivery and read are separate state transitions tracked per recipient, and offline users get a push notification with replay on reconnect.

The hardest scaling problem is that WebSockets are stateful: Rajesh's socket is on server A while Priya's message arrives on server B. Redis pub-sub bridges this by publishing to a per-user channel that the server holding the recipient's socket subscribes to. Sticky sessions keep reconnections landing on the same server. Deduplication with a client-generated message ID ensures retries never create duplicates.

Remember one sentence: Persist first so the database is the source of truth, deliver over full-duplex WebSockets with Redis pub-sub fan-out across servers, order per conversation with a sequence number, and fall back to push plus replay for offline users.
